proof_summary: For the small cases, direct minimality handles 9 and 27, while for 81 the congruence \(10^i\equiv1+9i\pmod{81}\), applied to a number and its reversal, forces the digit sum of any sub-\(10^9\) solution to be 0 or 81, hence the number is 0 or nine 9s. For \(n\ge5\), concatenate \(3^{n-5}\) copies of a 10-digit block whose value and reversal both have exact 3-adic valuation 5; the geometric repetition factor raises both valuations to \(n\), and the resulting \(10\cdot3^{n-5}\)-digit solution is shorter than the \(3^{n-2}\)-digit all-nines number.
